tax_exemption: Separate IRD endorsement under s.88 Inland Revenue Ordinance (charitable purpose, trust deed). Grants profits-tax exemption; donors deduct gifts up to 35% of assessable income. No VAT. Processing time unpublished.
No general charity tax regime. Foundations/associations apply to DSSCU for case-by-case profits-tax exemption; approval discretionary, timeline unpublished. No donor-deduction scheme exists in Macau.

Separate IPC endorsement from IRAS under s.37 Income Tax Act (Commissioner of Charities applies post-registration): full income-tax exemption; corporate donors get 250%, individuals 100% deduction. No VAT.

LHDN approval under s.44(6) Income Tax Act 1967 (charitable body, max 10 yrs) for income-tax exemption; approved-body donations deductible (individuals cap 10% of aggregate income). Application 1-3 months.

No separate application. Income used directly for non-distributive charitable activity is exempt from PPh (Art.4(3)); donations to recognized bodies deductible; most activities no VAT. Registration confers no tax status.

Foundation/association applies to Revenue Department for a tax-exemption certificate (income tax) before benefits; donors deduct gifts up to 10% of net income, some foundations double-deducted via e-Donation. No VAT.

Charitable fund (Decree 03/2026) gets fund income used for charitable purposes exempt from income tax; donors deduct up to 30% of taxable income. Exemption follows license, processed by tax authority within ~15-30 days.

BIR exemption ruling under s.30(E) NIRC required separately from SEC registration for income-tax exemption of donations; donor deduction capped at 20% of net income (itemized). Weeks to months; time unpublished.

No general charity tax regime. Associations/NGOs registered at Ministry of Interior must apply to GDT (MoEF) for case-by-case income-tax exemption; INGOs get duty-free import status via MoU. No standard donor deduction.

No charitable tax-exemption regime in the Income Tax Law. Exemptions only via investment promotion or special government approval, case-by-case; no public donor-deduction scheme. Social organisations pay standard CIT.

Non-profits register TIN with IRD, then apply to Director General for income-tax exemption certificate (Not 79/2020); donors deduct gifts to approved organisations subject to IRD caps. Months; time unpublished.

No personal income tax; corporate tax only. Charitable societies gain no automatic tax status on registration under Societies Act; exemption only by Minister's discretion under Income Tax Act. No donor-deduction regime.

Associations/foundations register with Ministry of Justice, then apply to the Tax Authority (ATT) for 10% income-tax exemption; approval case-by-case, time unpublished. No general donor-deduction scheme.

ACNC registration alone confers no tax benefit. ATO endorsement required separately: income-tax exemption, DGR status (donors claim 30% credit), GST/FBT concessions. DGR endorsement weeks to months; time unpublished.

Automatic: Charities Services notifies Inland Revenue on charity registration - income-tax exemption on charitable income follows; donee status (33 1/3% donor tax credit) then granted by IRD. Days to weeks; no VAT.

Automatic: entities registered under the Charitable Trusts Act are exempt from income tax without separate application (FRCS). Donors claim deduction for contributions to FRCS-listed approved charities. No VAT.

Non-profits must register a TIN with the IRC and apply for income-tax exemption from the IR (charitable purpose); donors deduct gifts of PGK50+ to qualifying charitable organisations. Approval time unpublished.

Income Tax Act 2012 gives donors a 30% tax credit for gifts to approved charitable institutions; the entity's own exemption is handled case-by-case by the Ministry for Revenue - process and time unpublished.

Charitable organisations are income-tax exempt (except business income) by Revenue Services under the Income Tax Act; donor deduction for registered charities. Application details and time unpublished.

No corporate income tax - no entity-level income tax, so registration with the VFSC (also Registrar of Charitable Organisations) needs no tax-exemption application. VAT exemptions cover some charitable supplies.
